title: Ostend: Maxim's Cabaret, Patrick's beating and Pollard's injury
summary: The Ostend engagement collapsed under a gambling owner; trombonist Jacob Patrick was clubbed by police and died months later, and Pollard was also injured in a brawl.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh yes, sure. And we went to -- after we did two months, May and June, two months, then we went to Pollard had an engagement in Ostend in a cabaret, Maxim's Cabaret, which did not do so well.
The proprietor, he had plenty of money, but he was a heavy gambler, and he took everything that he had. So, we found ourselves
Briggs

more or less on the street. But before that happened, within the first four weeks, our trombone player, Jacob Patrick, had an argument with some drunkard in the morning after work, maybe he was half high himself, I don't know, in a cabaret or something.

And he had a disturbance or fight or something, and they called the police and the police came -- when the police came, the police in Ostend speak Flemish, and poor Patrick he couldn't understand what was happening, and before anything happened, the guy just took his -- wham, on his shoulders.
With his club.
Whipped him to death. He was almost dead when we -- when someone saved him.
We were informed that he was in the hospital. We went to see him at the hospital, and he died six months after.
He did?
Briggs
Yes. But Ostend was a pretty bad place, because the leader, Pollard, he got into trouble too.
After we finished, we had enough money to stay around on vacation, you see. After the place folded, but we were not broke.
Pollard stayed and he liked to drink. He drank quite a lot. And they claim when he drank, he was annoying. They claim, I don't know, you see.
And he got into trouble, with some pimp broke a glass and just missed his vein, just missed him.
Just missed him?
Yes, just missed the temple. And that was another time, we got to go see him in the hospital.
Well, Pollard was what, he was Belgian, was he?
No, no. He was from Chicago.
Pollard?
Briggs
Yes, Chicago. FitzHugh Pollard.
But he hadn't been with the Southern Syncopators?
No, no, he came over on his own. He might have been -- the truth is, he might one of the 15th.
I see. Right.
'Cause they're quite a few of them, that just stayed over.
Yeh, just stayed.
He might have been, 'cause he was a wonderful musician.
